title: Fix the new product rows
prompt: Three new products must be added with exactly the same columns and types as `products`. The function below returns the right rows, but the check says the types are wrong. Fix `solve()`.
rules: `P023`, `Desk Mat`, `office`, active, with no price yet: its price is missing.
hints: Press Run and look at the schema of the result: what type did `unit_price` get?
With only column names, Spark guesses the types, and a number with a fraction becomes `double`. A schema string sets each type.
A `DECIMAL` column needs `Decimal` values, written from text so they stay exact: `Decimal("14.50")`. A float in a `DECIMAL` column is an error.
explanation: Passing only column names makes Spark guess every type, and `14.50` is a Python float, so `unit_price` comes out as `double`, not `decimal(10,2)`. The fix has two parts: a schema string that states each type, `"product_id STRING, name STRING, category STRING, unit_price DECIMAL(10,2), active BOOLEAN"`, and `Decimal("14.50")` and `Decimal("45.00")` for the prices, because a `DECIMAL` column won't take a float. Keep `None` for the missing price: a price of 0 would mean the mat is free.
